title: Trichotillomania
summary: Habitual hair pulling causing irregular patches of broken hairs. Habit-reversal therapy is first-line; watch for trichophagia and trichobezoar.

glance.think: Irregular or geometric bald patch with hairs of many different lengths; pull test negative; often on the dominant-hand side.
glance.engine: Body-focused repetitive behaviour (OCRD spectrum) — automatic or focused pulling; broken shafts, not autoimmune bulb attack.
glance.backbone: Non-judgemental recognition, habit-reversal / CBT referral, wound care if excoriated; do not treat as alopecia areata with steroids alone.
glance.never_miss: Trichophagia with abdominal pain, vomiting or mass → urgent surgical assessment for trichobezoar.

what: **Trichotillomania** (hair-pulling disorder) is a body-focused repetitive behaviour causing noticeable hair loss. It is not scarring in early disease. It is commoner in children and adolescents and often under-disclosed.

list: Classed with obsessive–compulsive related disorders; anxiety, boredom or sensory urge often precede pulling.
**Automatic** pulling (unaware, while reading/screens) vs **focused** pulling (conscious tension relief).
May coexist with skin picking or nail biting.
Irregular, angular or tonsure-like patches; hairs of **unequal lengths**; broken hairs firmly anchored.
Common sites: vertex, frontotemporal (dominant-hand side), brows and lashes.
Trichoscopy: black dots, broken hairs, **V-sign**, flame hairs — contrast with AA exclamation marks.
Chronic severe pulling can eventually scar; secondary infection/crust possible.

diagnosis: Clinical pattern ± behaviour history (ask privately, without blame). Pull test negative. Exclude tinea if scaly. Differentiate from [alopecia areata](condition:alopecia-areata) and [scarring alopecia](condition:scarring-alopecia).

head: Look-alike
Clues
rows: Smooth patch; exclamation hairs; positive edge pull test

list: Validate and reduce shame; involve parents/carers sensitively in children.
**Habit-reversal training / CBT** via CAMHS, psychology or specialist services is first-line.
Stimulus control (fidget tools, gloves at night, shorter nails); treat secondary infection if present.
Medicines are not first-line in primary care; any drug therapy is specialist.

red_flags: Abdominal pain, early satiety, vomiting, weight loss, halitosis, epigastric mass → urgent surgical review (trichobezoar / Rapunzel syndrome).
Self-harm or suicidal ideation → urgent mental-health assessment.
Diagnostic doubt or progressive scarring → dermatology.
pearls: Different hair lengths in one patch is the bedside clue.
Eyebrow/eyelash pulling in a child is still trichotillomania until proven otherwise — also consider AA and hypothyroidism for lateral brows.
Steroids will not fix the behaviour.
